title: Group Cohomology as a Derived Functor

items.title: Integral group-module and trivial-module convention
The invariants functor of a group module
Invariants are Hom from the trivial group-ring module
items.strategy: Evaluate a Z[G]-linear map at 1 and send an invariant to its unique Z-linear extension; check Z[G]-linearity and naturality in M.

items.title: The invariants functor is left exact
items.strategy: Transport established covariant Hom left exactness through the preceding natural isomorphism, keeping M in the second Hom variable.

items.title: Group cohomology as the right derived invariants functor
items.strategy: Fix H^n(G;M)=R^n((- )^G)(M), equivalently Ext^n over Z[G] from the trivial module under the supplied derived-resolution conventions. The later bar theorem supplies the projective calculation.

items.title: The coinvariants functor of a group module
The coinvariants functor is right exact
items.strategy: Use its quotient presentation, equivalently Z tensor over Z[G] minus, and the established right exactness of tensoring.

items.title: Group homology as the left derived coinvariants functor
items.strategy: Define H_n(G;M)=Tor_n^{Z[G]}(Z,M), deriving the right exact functor Z tensor over Z[G] minus; state the right trivial-module and left-coefficient handedness.

items.title: Degree-zero group cohomology and homology are invariants and coinvariants
items.strategy: Apply both degree-zero recovery theorems, then substitute the local definitions.

items.title: Long exact sequence in group cohomology
items.strategy: Specialize the cohomological delta-functor theorem for right derived functors to invariants, retaining the connecting maps and naturality.

items.title: Long exact sequence in group homology
items.strategy: Specialize the homological delta-functor theorem for left derived functors to coinvariants, including the degree direction of the connector.

items.title: Unnormalized homogeneous bar resolution
The bar differential is group equivariant and squares to zero
items.strategy: Diagonal equivariance is termwise; pair double deletions in the two possible orders to cancel the alternating faces.

items.title: Bar augmentation
The augmented bar complex is exact
items.strategy: After forgetting the G-action, insert the identity as leading vertex and verify the contraction equation. State explicitly that this contraction is only Z-linear.

items.title: The bar complex is a free resolution of the trivial module
items.strategy: Identify a free Z[G]-basis in every degree and combine it with exactness of the augmented complex; never call the underlying contraction equivariant.

items.title: Inhomogeneous group cochains
The inhomogeneous group-cochain differential squares to zero
items.strategy: Expand d squared and pair leading-action, adjacent-product, and terminal terms according to the two face deletions.

items.title: Homogeneous and inhomogeneous group cochains are isomorphic complexes
items.strategy: Print both inverse vertex/successive-quotient formulas, check G-equivariance, then verify every differential term.

items.title: The bar cochain complex computes derived group cohomology
items.strategy: Construct the specialized Hom balance comparison: for the free bar resolution P of Z and an injective resolution M to I, compare Hom(P,M) and Hom(Z,I) through the double complex Hom(P,I). Its two exactness directions give the required cohomology isomorphism, then use the homogeneous--inhomogeneous complex isomorphism.

items.title: Normalized bar resolution
Degenerate bar chains form a contractible subcomplex
items.strategy: Check the degenerate span is a subcomplex, then use signed degeneracy insertions to contract it.

items.title: Normalized and unnormalized bar complexes are chain-homotopy equivalent
items.strategy: Use the quotient by the contractible degenerate subcomplex, its splitting, and the contraction to build both homotopy identities.

items.title: Normalized cochains compute group cohomology
items.strategy: Apply Hom into M to the normalized--unnormalized homotopy equivalence and combine the resulting cohomology isomorphism with the bar-computation theorem.

items.title: Restriction, induction, and coinduction for group modules
Induction is left adjoint and coinduction right adjoint to restriction
items.strategy: Write the tensor--Hom adjunctions for Z[G] as a Z[G]-Z[H] bimodule, including the coinduction G-action and the unit/counit.

items.title: The group ring is free over a subgroup ring
items.strategy: Choose a coset transversal matching the module side and decompose group elements uniquely; record the choice dependence for arbitrary coset families.

items.title: Shapiro lemma for group cohomology
items.strategy: Use coinduction--restriction adjunction and subgroup freeness to identify the Hom cochain complexes naturally before passing to cohomology.

items.title: Shapiro lemma for group homology
items.strategy: Use induction, not coinduction, and identify the tensor complexes by associativity after transporting a projective resolution.

items.title: Cohomological dimension of a group
items.strategy: Define cd_Z(G) as the projective dimension of the trivial Z[G]-module, with least-resolution-length and infinity conventions stated.

items.title: Group cohomological dimension is detected by cohomology vanishing
items.strategy: Translate through H^n(G;M)=Ext^n_{Z[G]}(Z,M) and prove both implications by finite projective resolutions and the Ext/projective-dimension criterion, quantifying all M.

items.title: Restriction and corestriction on group cohomology
items.strategy: For finite-index H, define restriction by inclusion and corestriction by the finite coset sum on cochains, fixing a left transversal and the coefficient action.

items.title: Corestriction is independent of the coset representatives
items.strategy: Compare two transversals through H-valued correction factors, reindex the finite sum, and use H-equivariance to obtain the same cohomology map.

items.title: Restriction--corestriction composite is multiplication by the index
items.strategy: Expand corestriction after restriction on cochains; every coset summand is the original class. Give the reverse-composite normal/trivial-action refinement only in the sourced form.

items.title: Positive group cohomology of the trivial group vanishes
items.strategy: Specialize normalized bars to the trivial group, where all positive normalized chains vanish. This A-side lemma supplies transfer without a B-page dependency.

items.title: Finite groups have torsion annihilation in positive cohomology
items.strategy: Apply restriction--corestriction to the trivial subgroup; positive trivial-group cohomology vanishes, so |G| kills every positive cohomology class.

items.title: Groups of finite integral cohomological dimension are torsion free
items.strategy: Restrict a finite projective resolution to a hypothetical finite cyclic subgroup, construct its periodic resolution inline, and use its arbitrarily high nonvanishing to contradict finite cd. No B item is used.

items.title: FALSE: group cohomology is the derived functor of coinvariants
FALSE: the bar contracting homotopy is group equivariant
FALSE: H^1 is defined here as crossed homomorphisms modulo principal ones
FALSE: H^2 is defined here as equivalence classes of group extensions
FALSE: Shapiro lemma needs no distinction between induction and coinduction

title: Group Cohomology as a Derived Functor — Examples

items.title: Group cohomology of the trivial group
items.strategy: Use normalized bars to compute degree zero and all positive degrees for the trivial group.

items.title: Degree-zero invariants and coinvariants
items.strategy: Compute fixed points and the gm-minus-m quotient for a concrete action and identify them with H^0 and H_0.

items.title: The first three bar differentials
items.strategy: Write the degree-one, two, and three face formulas and exhibit an explicit cancellation.

items.title: Normalizing an inhomogeneous cochain
items.strategy: Subtract a degenerate contribution from a concrete low-degree cochain and verify the normalized representative.

items.title: A periodic resolution for a finite cyclic group
items.strategy: For C_m generated by t, verify the alternating t-minus-1 and norm maps form the standard free periodic resolution.

items.title: Cohomology of a finite cyclic group from the periodic resolution
items.strategy: Apply Hom over Z[C_m] into M and read off the alternating kernels and quotients of t-minus-1 and the norm.

items.title: Shapiro lemma for the trivial subgroup
items.strategy: Identify the induced and coinduced modules when H is trivial, then apply the two Shapiro theorems.

items.title: The underlying bar contraction is not equivariant
items.strategy: Compare the identity-insertion contraction on a bar generator with its translate for a nontrivial group.

items.title: Cohomological dimension of the trivial and infinite cyclic groups
items.strategy: Use the zero-length and t-minus-1 resolutions and give a coefficient module witnessing that cd(Z) is not zero.
